newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica coffee output seen down 6.2 pct - Icafe.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica coffee output seen down 6.2 pct - Icafe.

text.p: A report from Costa Rica Coffee Institute (Icafe) said Tuesday the first estimates for the 1996-1997 coffee crop calculate a fall in production of 6.2 percent from the output recorded in 1995-1996.

Causes of the expected dip in production to 2.3 million 60-kg bags from 2.6 million bags were given as a cyclical decline and damage from Hurricane Cesar that ravaged crop areas in the autumn, according to the Icafe report.
Edgar Rojas, deputy director of Icafe, said the fall in production was due to cyclical reasons but they were exacerbated by Hurricane Cesar.

Rojas said the final crop output could fall between 10 and 15 percent compared to 1995-1996 once further studies are completed on the ongoing crop "These circumstances make us believe that crop figures are still not definitive," he said.
The 1996-1997 cycle has not ended with harvesting still continuing in late maturing areas in the high altitude zones of the central coffee growing regions around San Jose, Heredia and Cartago.
Costa Rica's harvest starts in low lying plantations in June and picks up steam toward the end of each year (November-December) to finish in most parts around the end of February.
Cesar savaged Costa Rica, damaging plants and access roads, especially in the coffee gorwing regions of Perez Zeledon, the south of San Jose and Coto Brus and close to the border with Panama.
Infrastructure problems impeded bean picking at the time, Icafe officials said.
